items.title: Microsoft Surface GM on New AI PCs, 5G Devices and Surface Innovation
items.summary: In this NYSE Live interview, Sandra Andrews, General Manager of Microsoft Surface, discusses Microsoft's newest Surface devices and how the company is approaching the next generation of AI-enabled computing. Andrews provides an overview of the new Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch, highlighting their focus on portability, connectivity, performance, and AI readiness. She explains how the devices are designed to support a broad range of users seeking productive, mobile computing experiences across work and personal use cases. A significant portion of the discussion focuses on the evolution of AI-powered PCs. Andrews explains how modern hardware architectures now incorporate CPUs, GPUs, and dedicated Neural Processing Units (NPUs) to support emerging AI capabilities directly on the device. She discusses how these advancements help prepare users for increasingly sophisticated AI experiences while maintaining security, responsiveness, and efficiency. The interview also explores the importance of battery life and mobility. Andrews discusses how Microsoft's latest Surface devices are designed to deliver improved battery performance while remaining lightweight and portable. She explains why these features continue to be important for professionals, students, creators, and mobile workers. Another major theme is connectivity. Andrews highlights the benefits of built-in 5G capabilities, explaining how always-connected devices help users remain productive without depending on public Wi-Fi networks. She discusses Microsoft's focus on providing secure and reliable connectivity wherever users work. The conversation also covers Microsoft's new Surface Mouse and the introduction of haptic technology. Andrews explains how haptic feedback can create more intuitive interactions and enhance productivity experiences across the Windows ecosystem. Additionally, Andrews discusses Microsoft's engagement with the DPAA Global Video Everywhere Summit and shares how hands-on product experiences play an important role in helping customers understand the design, craftsmanship, and functionality of Surface hardware. Throughout the interview, Andrews provides perspectives on AI-powered computing, Surface devices, connectivity, mobility, user experience, hardware innovation, haptics, productivity technology, and the future of personal computing. Disclaimer: Informational content only. NYSE does not endorse or recommend investments, strategies, companies, products, or services discussed.

items.title: Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo on Tokenized Stocks and the Future of Capital Markets
items.summary: In this NYSE Live interview, Carlos Domingo, CEO of Securitize, discusses the company's recent launch of Securitize Stocks, the growth of tokenized assets, and the broader evolution of blockchain-based financial infrastructure. Domingo explains how Securitize Stocks is designed to provide eligible investors with access to tokenized U.S. equities through blockchain technology while preserving key elements of traditional ownership structures. He discusses the company's initial rollout and the vision for expanding access and functionality across a wider range of assets over time. A significant portion of the conversation focuses on the concept of tokenization and its role within modern capital markets. Domingo explains how blockchain-based representations of financial assets differ from synthetic products or derivatives and discusses the importance of maintaining shareholder-related rights and protections within tokenized structures. The interview also explores Securitize's collaboration with Ark Invest to bring the ARK Venture Fund on-chain. Domingo discusses how the fund provides exposure to a mix of public and private companies and highlights the growing interest in blockchain-enabled investment vehicles across the financial sector. Another major theme is institutional adoption. Domingo shares his perspective on how traditional asset managers, financial institutions, and market participants are increasingly exploring tokenization as a way to modernize financial products and market infrastructure. He discusses how industry attitudes toward blockchain technology have evolved and why tokenization is attracting greater attention from established financial organizations. The conversation further examines the technology required to support tokenized markets. Domingo discusses the importance of scalable blockchain networks, streamlined user experiences, and reducing friction associated with digital asset ownership. He emphasizes the need to make blockchain infrastructure largely invisible to end users while maintaining the benefits of the underlying technology. Additionally, the interview addresses the distinction between tokenization and cryptocurrency market movements. Domingo notes that tokenization focuses on modernizing the infrastructure underlying financial assets rather than relying on the price performance of digital currencies. Throughout the discussion, Domingo provides perspectives on blockchain technology, tokenized securities, financial innovation, digital asset infrastructure, investor access, market modernization, and the future of capital markets. Disclaimer: Informational content only. NYSE does not endorse or recommend investments, strategies, companies, products, or services discussed.
